* [Inbound Durability Hook](/advanced/inbound-durability) - At-least-once delivery with your backend

## Bounded pending-message storage

Message durability on [main snapshot `35a69a14`](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust/blob/35a69a14149fa2cd2a0cc719f875f441d1c6e1dc/wacore/src/store/traits.rs) requires more than the legacy pending-row getters and batch writes shown above. Implement these `ProtocolStore` operations explicitly:

| Operation | Required behavior |
| - | - |
| `read_pending_inbound_bounded` | Check length and read the same row snapshot before allocating. Oversized or non-BLOB data is an error; empty bytes are present data. |
| `read_pending_inbound_group_bounded` | Find a unique physical sender alias in one snapshot. Bound discovery to 400 keys of at most 128 bytes each and return the stored sender spelling. Reject ambiguity. |
| `replace_pending_inbound_if` | Compare the observed revision and replace atomically, with explicit expected absence and bounded payload sizes. |
| `delete_pending_inbound_if` | Delete only the observed bytes atomically. Preserve a conflicting successor row. |

There is no fallback from bounded reads to an unbounded getter. Retain the supplied `PendingInboundLease` through detached workers and retries, including after cancellation. The replacement payload owns its bytes and lease. Revision comparison alone does not prevent an absent-row ABA race after a successor creates and deletes a row; worker-terminal ownership is part of the contract.

Construction probes these operations and rejects unsupported durability backends. Passing the probe does not certify crash durability, batch atomicity, retention or cancellation safety. Exercise concurrent replacement, stale cleanup, alias conflicts and restart against your actual backend. A successful batch flush alone does not satisfy the conditional mutation contract.

## Session locking and Signal adapter failures

Custom `SendContextResolver` implementations must implement `lock_device_sessions`. Use the same canonical addresses and locks as direct sends, deduplicate targets and acquire locks in a stable order. Return a `SessionLockGuard` owning the locks until drop, including cancellation. `SessionLockGuard::none()` is valid only when the caller serializes every overlapping pairwise session operation. A sender-key lock alone does not protect pairwise ratchets.

The `Device` adapter returns an `io::ErrorKind::Unsupported` cause for signed-prekey enumeration, insertion and removal, sub-device session enumeration and bulk session deletion. These operations no longer report empty results or successful no-ops. `SignalProtocolStoreAdapter` likewise rejects `save_signed_pre_key`; `PersistenceManager` owns rotation. Successful session, identity and sender-key writes admit state to cache. Flush and propagate errors before relying on durability.

Default `SignalStore` batch methods run individual writes in order and stop at the first error. Earlier writes can already have committed. Backends used by `SignalStoreCache` must accept replay of the same snapshot after a failed flush. This does not authorize replay of an externally visible send.


# Group management
Source: https://whatsapp-rust.jlucaso.com/guides/group-management

Create a group and choose the least expensive projection for each task

<Note>
  Examples on this page target [source snapshot `35a69a14`](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust/tree/35a69a14149fa2cd2a0cc719f875f441d1c6e1dc), not a crates.io release. Use the [current API guide](/guides/current-api) to select the matching dependency.
</Note>

## Build a group input

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::{Client, GroupCreateOptions, GroupParticipantOptions, Jid};

async fn create(client: &Client, members: &[Jid]) -> whatsapp_rust::anyhow::Result<()> {
    let options = GroupCreateOptions::builder()
        .subject("Engineering")
        .participants(members.iter().cloned().map(GroupParticipantOptions::new).collect())
        .build();
    let created = client.groups().create_group(options).await?;
    println!("{}", created.metadata.id);
    Ok(())
}
```

The subject is required. For advanced policies, choose typed member-add, member-link and membership-approval modes on the builder or supported fields. Avoid downstream literals and `Default` for these non-exhaustive inputs.

## Separate listing from routing

List with `list_participating` and retrieve a subset with `fetch_overviews`. Fetch full metadata for participant roles, descriptions and other detailed state. Use `routing_info` for encryption membership. The [group task reference](/api/groups) explains network and cache differences and partial batch outcomes.

## Reconcile a description update

Use validated `GroupDescription` with `PreviousDescription::Resolve` when you do not have a fresh token. Use a known token explicitly when performing a compare-and-update. A conflict means the group changed; reread before deciding how to reconcile it.

## Handle participant results and history separately

Inspect each member result after adding, removing or changing admin roles. For history sharing, retain the prepared replay handle and call `deliver_prepared_history_share` again after cancellation. Use `retry_group_history` with a token from a retryable outcome; do not repeat the participant mutation. Cancellation can occur between remote operations; it does not roll them back.

## Look up pictures explicitly

Use `pictures().lookup(ProfilePictureRequest::new(ProfilePictureTarget::Group(group), size))` for one group. Use `Community` for a community parent. The separate `get_profile_pictures` batch remains on the groups facade.

See [group operations](/api/groups), [community tasks](/api/community), [pictures](/api/pictures) and [current API contracts](/guides/current-api).


# Media Handling
Source: https://whatsapp-rust.jlucaso.com/guides/media-handling

Learn how to upload and download media with encryption in whatsapp-rust

## Overview

This guide covers uploading and downloading media (images, videos, audio, documents, stickers) with automatic encryption and decryption.

## Downloading Media

### From message objects

Download media directly from message types that implement `Downloadable`:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::Downloadable;
use whatsapp_rust::client::Client;
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::types::events::InboundMessage;

match event {
    Event::Messages(batch) => {
        for InboundMessage { message, info, .. } in batch.iter() {
            // Image
            if let Some(img) = message.image_message.as_option() {
                let data = client.download(img, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
                std::fs::write("image.jpg", data)?;
            }

            // Video
            if let Some(video) = message.video_message.as_option() {
                let data = client.download(video, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
                std::fs::write("video.mp4", data)?;
            }

            // Audio
            if let Some(audio) = message.audio_message.as_option() {
                let data = client.download(audio, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
                let ext = if audio.ptt() { "ogg" } else { "mp3" };
                std::fs::write(format!("audio.{}", ext), data)?;
            }

            // Document
            if let Some(doc) = message.document_message.as_option() {
                let data = client.download(doc, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
                let filename = doc.file_name.as_deref().unwrap_or("document");
                std::fs::write(filename, data)?;
            }

            // Sticker
            if let Some(sticker) = message.sticker_message.as_option() {
                let data = client.download(sticker, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
                std::fs::write("sticker.webp", data)?;
            }
        }
    }
    _ => {}
}
```

See [Download API reference](/api/download) for full details.

### Streaming Download

For large files, use streaming to avoid memory overhead:

```rust theme={null}
use std::fs::File;

if let Some(video) = message.video_message.as_option() {
    let file = File::create("video.mp4")?;
    let file = client.download_to_writer(video, file, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
    println!("Video downloaded and verified");
}
```

See [Download API reference](/api/download#download_to_writer) for streaming details.

<Note>
  With a streaming HTTP adapter and a file destination, `download_to_writer` keeps bounded crypto/read state. This excludes adapter/TLS buffers and destination storage. With default limits, non-streaming adapters can buffer the whole response before writing it. Explicit byte limits require streaming and refuse a non-streaming adapter before HTTP. See [download limits](/api/download#download-byte-limits).
</Note>

### From raw parameters

Download media when you have the raw encryption parameters:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;
use whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadParams;

let params = DownloadParams::encrypted(
    "/v/t62.1234-5/...",  // direct_path
    &media_key,            // media_key (32 bytes)
    &file_sha256,          // file_sha256
    &file_enc_sha256,      // file_enc_sha256
    12345,                 // file_length
    MediaType::Image,      // media_type
)?;

let data = client.download(&params, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;

std::fs::write("downloaded.jpg", data)?;
```

See [Download API reference](/api/download#download) for raw parameter downloads.

### Streaming from raw parameters

```rust theme={null}
let params = DownloadParams::encrypted(
    direct_path,
    &media_key,
    &file_sha256,
    &file_enc_sha256,
    file_length,
    MediaType::Video,
)?;

let file = File::create("large_video.mp4")?;
let file = client.download_to_writer(&params, file, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
```

See [Download API reference](/api/download#download_to_writer) for streaming from raw parameters.

### Downloading without an active session

`Client::download` and its variants need a connected `Client` for most media; they ask the server for CDN hosts (cached and refreshed automatically, not fetched on every call). The exception is `static_url` media (newsletter/channel content), which skips that entirely; see the [Download API reference](/api/download#download) for details. If you've persisted a message's CDN fields (for example as a [`DownloadParams`](/api/download#downloadparams)) and want to fetch that media later, after the session that received it has disconnected, use [`MediaDownloader`](/api/download#mediadownloader) instead. It needs only an `HttpClient` and a `Runtime`; no `Client`, no pairing:

```rust theme={null}
use std::sync::Arc;
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;
use whatsapp_rust::download::{DownloadParams, MediaDownloader};

// Same HttpClient/Runtime you'd pass to ClientBuilder — no session required.
let downloader = MediaDownloader::with_default_hosts(http_client.clone(), runtime.clone());

let params = DownloadParams::encrypted(
    direct_path,
    &media_key,
    &file_sha256,
    &file_enc_sha256,
    file_length,
    MediaType::Image,
)?;

let data = downloader.download(&params, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
```

<Note>
  `MediaDownloader` uses the same streaming/buffered behavior and host failover as client downloads. It cannot refresh the host list through a session. A reference rejection returns a typed [`MediaDownloadError`](/api/download#mediadownloaderror). Supply hosts with `MediaRoute::new(hosts)` or use the default-host convenience; download routes carry no auth token.
</Note>

## Thumbnails

Thumbnails are **not generated by the library** — you provide them as raw JPEG bytes when constructing media messages. WhatsApp clients use these thumbnails as low-resolution previews while the full media is downloading.

### Setting thumbnails on media messages

Set the `jpeg_thumbnail` field on image, video, or document messages:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::waproto::whatsapp as wa;

let upload = client.upload(image_data, MediaType::Image, Default::default()).await?;

let message = {
    let mut value = wa::Message::default();
    value.image_message = buffa::MessageField::some({
        let mut value = wa::message::ImageMessage::default();
        value.url = Some(upload.url.clone());
        value.direct_path = Some(upload.direct_path.clone());
        value.media_key = Some(upload.media_key_vec());
        value.file_sha256 = Some(upload.file_sha256_vec());
        value.file_enc_sha256 = Some(upload.file_enc_sha256_vec());
        value.file_length = Some(upload.file_length);
        value.media_key_timestamp = Some(upload.media_key_timestamp);
        value.mimetype = Some("image/jpeg".to_string());
        value.jpeg_thumbnail = Some(thumbnail_bytes); // Raw JPEG bytes
        value.width = Some(1920);
        value.height = Some(1080);
        value
    });
    value
};
```

### Thumbnail fields by message type

| Message type | Inline thumbnail field | Server-hosted thumbnail fields |
| - | - | - |
| `ImageMessage` | `jpeg_thumbnail` | `thumbnail_direct_path`, `thumbnail_sha256`, `thumbnail_enc_sha256` |
| `VideoMessage` | `jpeg_thumbnail` | `thumbnail_direct_path`, `thumbnail_sha256`, `thumbnail_enc_sha256` |
| `DocumentMessage` | `jpeg_thumbnail` | `thumbnail_direct_path`, `thumbnail_sha256`, `thumbnail_enc_sha256` |
| `StickerMessage` | `png_thumbnail` | — |

<Note>
  Inline thumbnails (`jpeg_thumbnail` / `png_thumbnail`) are embedded directly in the encrypted message payload. Server-hosted thumbnail fields (`thumbnail_direct_path`, etc.) reference a separately uploaded thumbnail that clients can download independently. For most use cases, inline thumbnails are sufficient.
</Note>

### Reusing thumbnails from incoming messages

When re-uploading media (for example, after processing or transcoding), you can clone the thumbnail from the original message:

```rust theme={null}
if let Some(img) = message.image_message.as_option() {
    let data = client.download(img, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
    let upload = client.upload(data, MediaType::Image, Default::default()).await?;

    let reply = {
        let mut value = wa::Message::default();
        value.image_message = buffa::MessageField::some({
            let mut value = wa::message::ImageMessage::default();
            value.url = Some(upload.url.clone());
            value.direct_path = Some(upload.direct_path.clone());
            value.media_key = Some(upload.media_key_vec());
            value.file_sha256 = Some(upload.file_sha256_vec());
            value.file_enc_sha256 = Some(upload.file_enc_sha256_vec());
            value.file_length = Some(upload.file_length);
            value.media_key_timestamp = Some(upload.media_key_timestamp);
            value.mimetype = img.mimetype.clone();
            value.jpeg_thumbnail = img.jpeg_thumbnail.clone(); // Reuse from original
            value.height = img.height;
            value.width = img.width;
            value
        });
        value
    };
}
```

<Tip>
  If you don't need to modify the media, use [CDN reuse](#forwarding-media-via-cdn-reuse) instead — it forwards the entire message (including thumbnails) without downloading or re-uploading anything.
</Tip>

### Downloading link thumbnails

The `LinkThumbnail` variant in `MediaType` supports downloading thumbnails for URL previews in `ExtendedTextMessage`:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;
use whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadParams;

// LinkThumbnail uses HKDF info "WhatsApp Link Thumbnail Keys"
let params = DownloadParams::encrypted(
    thumbnail_direct_path,
    &thumbnail_media_key,
    &thumbnail_sha256,
    &thumbnail_enc_sha256,
    thumbnail_length,
    MediaType::LinkThumbnail,
)?;

let thumbnail = client.download(&params, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
```

## Forwarding media via CDN reuse

When you receive a media message (image, video, audio, document, sticker), you can "forward" it by reusing the original CDN fields directly — no download or re-upload needed. This is instant regardless of file size because no media bytes are transferred.

The technique works because every media message contains all the CDN metadata (`url`, `direct_path`, `media_key`, `file_sha256`, etc.) needed for recipients to fetch the blob. You simply clone those fields into a new `wa::Message` and call `send_message`:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::waproto::whatsapp as wa;

/// Reuses the original CDN blob, only swaps the caption.
/// Instant regardless of file size — no download or re-upload.
fn forward_image(original: &wa::message::ImageMessage) -> wa::Message {
    {
        let mut value = wa::Message::default();
        value.image_message = buffa::MessageField::some({
            let mut value = original.clone(); // Preserve the original media metadata.
            value.caption = Some("Forwarded image".to_string());
            value
        });
        value
    }
}

// In your message handler:
if let Some(img) = message.image_message.as_option() {
    let forwarded = forward_image(img);
    client.send_message(destination_jid, forwarded).await?;
}
```

The same pattern works for any media type:

```rust theme={null}
// Forward a video, keeping all CDN fields intact
if let Some(vid) = message.video_message.as_option() {
    let forwarded = {
        let mut value = wa::Message::default();
        value.video_message = buffa::MessageField::some({
            let mut value = vid.clone();
            value.caption = Some("Forwarded video".to_string());
            value
        });
        value
    };
    client.send_message(destination_jid, forwarded).await?;
}
```

<Tip>
  Only use `download` + `upload` when you need the plaintext bytes (processing, transcoding, re-encoding). To forward existing media unchanged, reuse the original message's CDN fields directly.
</Tip>

### When CDN reuse won't work

CDN URLs expire after some time. If the original media URL has expired, recipients won't be able to download it. In that case, use [media reupload](/api/client#media_reupload) to request the server to provide a fresh download path, or fall back to downloading and re-uploading the media.

## Uploading Media

### Basic Upload

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;
use whatsapp_rust::upload::UploadResponse;

// Read file data
let data = std::fs::read("photo.jpg")?;

// Upload with automatic encryption
let upload: UploadResponse = client.upload(data, MediaType::Image, Default::default()).await?;

println!("URL: {}", upload.url);
println!("Direct path: {}", upload.direct_path);
println!("File SHA256: {:?}", upload.file_sha256);
```

See [Upload API reference](/api/upload) for full details.

### Using upload response in messages

The `whatsapp_rust::media` module turns an `UploadResponse` into a ready-to-send `wa::Message`, so you don't hand-assemble the CDN/crypto fields (url, direct\_path, media\_key, the two SHA-256 hashes, file\_length, media\_key\_timestamp, streaming\_sidecar):

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;
use whatsapp_rust::media::{self, ImageOptions};

let upload = client.upload(image_data, MediaType::Image, Default::default()).await?;

let message = media::image_message(upload, {
    let mut options = ImageOptions::default();
    options.caption = Some("Check out this image!".to_string());
    options
});

let result = client.send_message(to, message).await?;
```

`media::video_message`, `media::document_message`, and `media::audio_message` work the same way with their own options structs (and carry the streaming sidecar for video/audio). See [media message builders](/api/upload#high-level-message-builders).

<Accordion title="Building the message by hand">
  You can still assemble the proto yourself when you need a field the options structs don't expose (e.g. explicit `width`/`height`):

  ```rust theme={null}
  use whatsapp_rust::waproto::whatsapp as wa;

  let upload = client.upload(image_data, MediaType::Image, Default::default()).await?;

  let message = {
      let mut value = wa::Message::default();
      value.image_message = buffa::MessageField::some({
          let mut value = wa::message::ImageMessage::default();
          value.url = Some(upload.url.clone());
          value.direct_path = Some(upload.direct_path.clone());
          value.media_key = Some(upload.media_key_vec());
          value.file_sha256 = Some(upload.file_sha256_vec());
          value.file_enc_sha256 = Some(upload.file_enc_sha256_vec());
          value.file_length = Some(upload.file_length);
          value.media_key_timestamp = Some(upload.media_key_timestamp);
          value.mimetype = Some("image/jpeg".to_string());
          value.caption = Some("Check out this image!".to_string());
          value.width = Some(1920);
          value.height = Some(1080);
          value
      });
      value
  };

  let result = client.send_message(to, message).await?;
  ```
</Accordion>

### Sending media as an album

You can group multiple images and/or videos into an album. See [Sending Messages - Album messages](/guides/sending-messages#album-messages) for a full walkthrough of the parent/child album pattern using `AlbumMessage` and `wrap_as_album_child`.

### Resumable uploads

For files 5 MiB or larger, the client automatically checks whether a previous upload of the same file exists on the CDN before uploading the full payload. This avoids re-uploading data that the server already has.

The resume check flow works as follows:

1. The client sends a `?resume=1` probe to the CDN for each host
2. If the server responds with **complete**, the existing URL is returned immediately — no upload occurs
3. If the server responds with a **byte offset**, only the remaining bytes are uploaded using the `file_offset` query parameter
4. If the server responds with **not found** (or the check fails), a full upload proceeds

<Note>
  Resumable upload detection is fully transparent. You call `client.upload()` the same way regardless of file size. The resume check is non-fatal — if it fails for any reason, the client falls back to a full upload.
</Note>

```rust theme={null}
// Large files automatically use resumable upload logic
let video_bytes = std::fs::read("large_video.mp4")?; // e.g., 50 MiB
let upload = client.upload(video_bytes, MediaType::Video, Default::default()).await?;
// If a partial upload existed, only the remaining bytes were sent
```

## Media Types

### Available media types

```rust theme={null}
pub enum MediaType {
    Image,
    Video,
    Audio,
    Document,
    History,
    AppState,
    Sticker,
    StickerPack,
    StickerPackThumbnail,
    LinkThumbnail,
    ProductCatalogImage,
    MusicArtwork,
    NewsletterMusicArtwork,
}
```

### Media type properties

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;

// Get MMS type for upload URLs
let mms_type = MediaType::Image.mms_type();
// Returns: "image", "video", "audio", "document"

// Get app info string for HKDF key derivation
let info = MediaType::Video.app_info();
// Returns: "WhatsApp Video Keys"

// Get upload path for CDN routing
let path = MediaType::Image.upload_path();
// Returns: "/mms/image"

// Check if media type uses E2E encryption
let encrypted = MediaType::ProductCatalogImage.is_encrypted();
// Returns: false (product catalog images are unencrypted)
```

<Note>
  `ProductCatalogImage` and `NewsletterMusicArtwork` are explicitly plaintext media types. For downloads of other types, key presence selects encryption, except `MusicArtwork`, which always requires it. Use `DownloadParams::plaintext` for stored newsletter metadata without a key. Product catalog images upload to `/product/image`.
</Note>

## Encryption Details

### Upload Encryption

Media is automatically encrypted before upload:

1. Generate random 32-byte `media_key`
2. Derive encryption keys using HKDF-SHA256:
   * IV: 16 bytes
   * Cipher key: 32 bytes
   * MAC key: 32 bytes
3. Encrypt with AES-256-CBC
4. Append HMAC-SHA256 MAC (10 bytes)
5. Compute SHA256 hashes of plaintext and ciphertext

```rust theme={null}
// Encryption happens automatically in upload()
let data = std::fs::read("file.pdf")?;
let upload = client.upload(data, MediaType::Document, Default::default()).await?;

// The UploadResponse contains all encryption metadata
// media_key, file_sha256, file_enc_sha256 are [u8; 32] arrays
println!("Media key: {:?}", upload.media_key);
println!("File length: {} bytes", upload.file_length);
```

### Chunk-based encryption with MediaEncryptor

`MediaEncryptor` provides a chunk-based API for encrypting media incrementally. Unlike `encrypt_media_streaming`, it doesn't require a sync `Read` source — you can feed plaintext in arbitrarily sized chunks, making it suitable for async streams and network sources:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::upload::MediaEncryptor;
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;

let mut enc = MediaEncryptor::new(MediaType::Video)?;
let mut encrypted = Vec::new();

// Feed plaintext in any chunk size
for chunk in video_chunks {
    enc.update(&chunk, &mut encrypted);
}

// Finalize: PKCS7 pad + append 10-byte HMAC-SHA256 MAC
let info = enc.finalize(&mut encrypted)?;
// info.media_key, info.file_sha256, info.file_enc_sha256, info.file_length
```

You can also write directly to a file or writer instead of buffering in memory:

```rust theme={null}
let mut enc = MediaEncryptor::new(MediaType::Video)?;
let mut writer = File::create("large_video.enc")?;

for chunk in video_chunks {
    enc.update_to_writer(&chunk, &mut writer)?;
}

let info = enc.finalize_to_writer(&mut writer)?;
```

See [Upload API reference](/api/upload#mediaencryptor) for full details.

### Streaming encryption from a reader

For sync `Read` sources, `encrypt_media_streaming` wraps `MediaEncryptor` and reads in 8KB chunks:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::upload::encrypt_media_streaming;
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::MediaType;
use std::fs::File;

let reader = File::open("large_video.mp4")?;
let writer = File::create("large_video.enc")?;

let info = encrypt_media_streaming(reader, writer, MediaType::Video)?;
// info.media_key, info.file_sha256, info.file_enc_sha256, info.file_length
```

See [Upload API reference](/api/upload#streaming-encryption) for full details.

### Download Decryption

Decryption is automatic when downloading:

1. Fetch encrypted data from WhatsApp CDN
2. Verify MAC (last 10 bytes)
3. Decrypt with AES-256-CBC
4. Verify plaintext SHA256
5. Return decrypted data

```rust theme={null}
// Decryption happens automatically in download()
let data = client.download(image_message, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
// `data` is already decrypted and verified
```

<Warning>
  Never skip SHA256 verification! The library automatically verifies both encrypted and decrypted hashes to ensure data integrity.
</Warning>

## Error Handling

### Download Errors

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::{Client, download::{ClientDownloadError, Downloadable}};

async fn safe_download(
    client: &Client,
    downloadable: &dyn Downloadable,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientDownloadError> {
    match client.download(downloadable, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await {
        Ok(data) => Ok(data),
        Err(error) => {
            match &error {
                ClientDownloadError::ReferenceRejected(_) => eprintln!("Media reference rejected"),
                ClientDownloadError::Preparation(_) => eprintln!("Invalid media metadata"),
                _ => eprintln!("Download failed: {error:?}"),
            }
            Err(error)
        }
    }
}
```

Download errors redact opaque backend text in `Display` and `Debug`. Match typed variants instead of parsing diagnostic strings. Explicit access to the source chain can expose signed URLs; see [safe diagnostics](/api/download#safe-diagnostics).

### Upload Errors

```rust theme={null}
async fn safe_upload(
    client: &Client,
    data: Vec<u8>,
    media_type: MediaType,
) -> Result<UploadResponse> {
    match client.upload(data, media_type, Default::default()).await {
        Ok(upload) => {
            println!("✅ Uploaded to: {}", upload.url);
            Ok(upload)
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("Upload failed"); // The returned source may contain signed URLs.
            Err(e)
        }
    }
}
```

## Advanced Usage

### Custom media processing

```rust theme={null}
use image::DynamicImage;

// Download and process image
if let Some(img) = message.image_message.as_option() {
    let data = client.download(img, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
    
    // Load with image crate
    let image = image::load_from_memory(&data)?;
    
    // Resize
    let thumbnail = image.resize(200, 200, image::imageops::FilterType::Lanczos3);
    
    // Save
    thumbnail.save("thumbnail.jpg")?;
}
```

### Streaming with Progress

When you pass a writer to `download_to_writer`, you must implement [`DownloadWriter`](/api/download#downloadwriter-trait), not just `Write + Seek` — see that reference for why. For a wrapper like this one, the impl is a one-line delegation to the inner writer, plus resetting your own tracked state to match:

```rust theme={null}
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Write, Seek};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use whatsapp_rust::wacore::download::DownloadWriter;

struct ProgressWriter<W> {
    inner: W,
    total: Arc<Mutex<usize>>,
}

impl<W: Write> Write for ProgressWriter<W> {
    fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
        let n = self.inner.write(buf)?;
        *self.total.lock().unwrap() += n;
        println!("Downloaded {} bytes", *self.total.lock().unwrap());
        Ok(n)
    }
    
    fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.inner.flush()
    }
}

impl<W: Seek> Seek for ProgressWriter<W> {
    fn seek(&mut self, pos: std::io::SeekFrom) -> std::io::Result<u64> {
        self.inner.seek(pos)
    }
}

impl<W: DownloadWriter> DownloadWriter for ProgressWriter<W> {
    fn truncate(&mut self, len: u64) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        self.inner.truncate(len)?;
        // download_to_writer truncates to 0 at the start of every attempt
        // (including retries after a failed host), so the counter has to
        // follow along or it double-counts bytes from an attempt that failed.
        *self.total.lock().unwrap() = len as usize;
        Ok(())
    }
}

let file = File::create("video.mp4")?;
let progress_writer = ProgressWriter {
    inner: file,
    total: Arc::new(Mutex::new(0)),
};

let _file = client.download_to_writer(video, progress_writer, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
```

### Automatic retry and failover

For session-derived download routes, HTTP 401 can trigger one media-session refresh and URL re-derivation with refreshed hosts. HTTP 403/404/410 are terminal reference rejections; refreshing hosts cannot renew a signed reference. Download routes carry no auth token. Static URLs bypass session refresh, and `MediaDownloader` returns a reference rejection immediately because it has no session.

Transport, HTTP, or integrity failures can fall over to another host. Local writer failures are terminal. Inspect the typed [download errors](/api/download#clientdownloaderror) and publish the destination only after success; cleanup after cancellation is not guaranteed.

Upload retains its authentication token and credential-refresh behavior. See [upload](/api/upload) for that separate path.

### Additional retry logic

For transient errors beyond reference rejections, you can implement your own retry wrapper:

```rust theme={null}
use tokio::time::{sleep, Duration};
use whatsapp_rust::{Client, download::{ClientDownloadError, Downloadable}};

async fn download_with_retry(
    client: &Client,
    downloadable: &dyn Downloadable,
    max_retries: u32,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ClientDownloadError> {
    let mut attempt = 0;
    loop {
        match client.download(downloadable, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await {
            Ok(data) => return Ok(data),
            Err(e @ ClientDownloadError::HostsUnreachable(_)) if attempt < max_retries => {
                attempt += 1;
                eprintln!("Retry {}/{}: {:?}", attempt, max_retries, e);
                sleep(Duration::from_secs(2u64.pow(attempt))).await;
            }
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
    }
}
```

## Media connection

### Automatic management

The client caches media connection information. Downloads use its CDN hosts; uploads also use its authentication token. Session-derived downloads can refresh hosts once after HTTP 401. HTTP 403/404/410 are terminal for downloads, while uploads refresh credentials on 401/403:

```rust theme={null}
// Each operation applies its own refresh policy
let upload = client.upload(data, MediaType::Image, Default::default()).await?;
let download = client.download(downloadable, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;

// The client manages the cached media connection.
```

### Host types and failover order

Each media connection includes multiple CDN hosts with a `host_type` field indicating whether the host is `"primary"` or `"fallback"`. The client sorts hosts with primary hosts first, so uploads and downloads always try the fastest hosts before falling back to alternatives. Each host may also include a `fallback_hostname` for additional resilience.

### Cache expiration

Media connections have two TTL values:

* **`ttl`** — how long the route/host information is valid
* **`auth_ttl`** — how long the auth token specifically is valid (may be shorter than `ttl`)

The client uses the minimum of these two values to determine when the cached connection has expired. When expired, the next session-derived media operation fetches fresh connection information. Download routes retain only its hosts.

### Internal refresh

Media connection refresh and invalidation are managed internally by the client. Download refresh updates hosts and re-derives the URL without adding an auth token. Static download URLs bypass session refresh, and standalone `MediaDownloader` has no session to refresh. Upload credential refresh remains separate.

## Best Practices

<Steps>
  ### Use streaming for large files

  ```rust theme={null}
  // ❌ Bad: Loads entire file into memory
  let data = client.download(video, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
  std::fs::write("video.mp4", data)?;

  // ✅ Good: Constant memory usage (with streaming HTTP client)
  let file = File::create("video.mp4")?;
  let _file = client.download_to_writer(video, file, whatsapp_rust::download::DownloadLimits::default()).await?;
  ```

  <Note>
    `download_to_writer` uses bounded crypto/read state with streaming adapters; adapter buffers and destination storage are separate. With non-streaming clients, unbounded calls fall back to buffered downloads. Bounded calls require streaming. See [byte limits](/api/download#download-byte-limits).
  </Note>

  ### Verify media type

  Check `mimetype` before processing:

  ```rust theme={null}
  if let Some(img) = message.image_message.as_option() {
      if let Some(mimetype) = &img.mimetype {
          match mimetype.as_str() {
              "image/jpeg" | "image/png" => {
                  // Process image
              }
              _ => {
                  eprintln!("Unsupported image type: {}", mimetype);
              }
          }
      }
  }
  ```

  ### Handle missing fields

  Media messages may have optional fields:

  ```rust theme={null}
  if let Some(doc) = message.document_message.as_option() {
      let filename = doc.file_name.as_deref().unwrap_or("unknown");
      let mimetype = doc.mimetype.as_deref().unwrap_or("application/octet-stream");
      let size = doc.file_length.unwrap_or(0);
      
      println!("Document: {} ({}, {} bytes)", filename, mimetype, size);
  }
  ```

  ### Set proper dimensions

  For images and videos, include dimensions:

  ```rust theme={null}
  use image::GenericImageView;

  let img = image::open("photo.jpg")?;
  let (width, height) = img.dimensions();

  let message = {
      let mut value = wa::Message::default();
      value.image_message = buffa::MessageField::some({
          let mut value = wa::message::ImageMessage::default();
          value.url = Some(upload.url.clone());
          value.direct_path = Some(upload.direct_path.clone());
          value.media_key = Some(upload.media_key_vec());
          value.file_sha256 = Some(upload.file_sha256_vec());
          value.file_enc_sha256 = Some(upload.file_enc_sha256_vec());
          value.file_length = Some(upload.file_length);
          value.media_key_timestamp = Some(upload.media_key_timestamp);
          value.mimetype = Some("image/jpeg".to_string());
          value.width = Some(width);
          value.height = Some(height);
          value
      });
      value
  };
  ```
</Steps>

# Newsletters (channels)
Source: https://whatsapp-rust.jlucaso.com/guides/newsletters

Learn how to create, manage, and interact with WhatsApp newsletter channels in whatsapp-rust

<Note>
  Examples on this page target [source snapshot `35a69a14`](https://github.com/oxidezap/whatsapp-rust/tree/35a69a14149fa2cd2a0cc719f875f441d1c6e1dc), not a crates.io release. Use the [current API guide](/guides/current-api) to select the matching dependency.
</Note>

## Overview

Newsletters (also called channels) are broadcast-style messaging in WhatsApp. Unlike groups, newsletter messages are **plaintext** (no Signal E2E encryption) and flow one-way from admins to subscribers.

This guide covers creating newsletters, managing subscriptions, sending messages, and handling live updates.

## Accessing the Newsletter API

All newsletter operations are accessed through the `newsletter()` method:

```rust theme={null}
let newsletter = client.newsletter();
```

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter) for the full API.

## Creating a newsletter

```rust theme={null}
let created = client.newsletter()
    .create("My Channel", Some("Channel description"))
    .await?;

println!("Created: {} ({})", created.name, created.jid);
println!("Invite code: {:?}", created.invite_code);
```

The returned `NewsletterMetadata` contains the channel's JID (with `@newsletter` server), name, subscriber count, and invite code.

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter#create) for details.

## Listing subscribed newsletters

```rust theme={null}
let newsletters = client.newsletter().list_subscribed().await?;

for nl in &newsletters {
    println!("{}: {} ({} subscribers)",
        nl.jid, nl.name, nl.subscriber_count);
}
```

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter#list_subscribed) for details.

## Fetching metadata

### By JID

```rust theme={null}
let metadata = client.newsletter().get_metadata(&newsletter_jid).await?;

println!("Name: {}", metadata.name);
println!("Description: {:?}", metadata.description);
println!("Subscribers: {}", metadata.subscriber_count);
println!("Verification: {:?}", metadata.verification);
println!("State: {:?}", metadata.state);
```

### By invite code

```rust theme={null}
let metadata = client.newsletter()
    .get_metadata_by_invite("invite-code-here")
    .await?;

println!("Found: {} ({})", metadata.name, metadata.jid);
```

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter#get_metadata) for all metadata fields.

## Joining and leaving

### Join a newsletter

```rust theme={null}
let joined = client.newsletter().join(&newsletter_jid).await?;

println!("Joined '{}' as {:?}", joined.name, joined.role);
```

### Leave a newsletter

```rust theme={null}
client.newsletter().leave(&newsletter_jid).await?;
```

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter#join) for details.

## Updating a newsletter

You can update the name and/or description of a newsletter you own:

```rust theme={null}
let updated = client.newsletter()
    .update(
        &newsletter_jid,
        Some("New Channel Name"),
        Some("Updated description"),
    )
    .await?;

println!("Updated: {}", updated.name);
```

Pass `None` for fields you don't want to change.

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter#update) for details.

## Sending messages

Newsletter messages are plaintext — they bypass Signal encryption entirely. You send newsletter messages through the unified `client.send_message()` method, just like regular and group messages.

### Text messages

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::waproto::whatsapp as wa;

let mut message = wa::Message::default();
message.conversation = Some("Hello subscribers!".to_string());

let msg_id = client.send_message(newsletter_jid, message).await?;

println!("Sent message: {}", msg_id);
```

The library automatically detects that the recipient is a newsletter JID and sends the message as plaintext (no Signal encryption). It also infers the correct `type` attribute (text, media, reaction, poll) and `mediatype` attribute from the message content. Stanza-level `<meta>` nodes (for polls, events, etc.) are also injected automatically, matching WhatsApp Web behavior.

<Note>
  For media messages (images, videos, etc.), you must upload the media separately using the newsletter-specific upload endpoint before sending. Text messages work directly.
</Note>

### Reactions, votes, edits and revokes

For a fetched newsletter message, use `message.message_ref(&newsletter_jid)?`; for an inbound envelope use `inbound.newsletter_ref()?`. Pass the result to the newsletter facade.

Reactions and poll votes use its server content ID and return a new operation `StanzaId`. Edits and revokes use its client content `MessageId`. The IDs are independent and optional; a missing required domain is rejected, not guessed from another field. Use the [newsletter action examples](/api/newsletter#send_reaction) and [migration guide](/guides/current-api#message-actions-and-identity).

## Fetching message history

Retrieve past messages with pagination support:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::NewsletterMessageType;
use wacore::types::message::EditAttribute;

// Fetch the latest 50 messages
let messages = client.newsletter()
    .get_messages(&newsletter_jid, 50, None)
    .await?;

for msg in &messages {
    println!("ID: {}, time: {}, type: {:?}",
        msg.server_id, msg.timestamp, msg.message_type);

    match msg.edit {
        EditAttribute::AdminEdit => println!("  (edited)"),
        EditAttribute::AdminRevoke => println!("  (revoked)"),
        _ => {}
    }

    if let Some(decoded) = &msg.message {
        if let Some(text) = &decoded.conversation {
            println!("  Text: {}", text);
        }
    }

    for reaction in &msg.reactions {
        println!("  {} x{}", reaction.code, reaction.count);
    }

    if msg.message_type == NewsletterMessageType::Poll {
        for vote in &msg.votes {
            println!("  poll option {}: {}", hex::encode(vote.option_hash), vote.count);
        }
    }

    if let Some(forwards) = msg.forwards_count {
        println!("  forwards: {}", forwards);
    }
}
```

Each [`NewsletterMessage`](/api/newsletter#newslettermessage) also carries the message's `message_id` (for [`edit_message`](/api/newsletter#edit_message) and [`revoke_message`](/api/newsletter#revoke_message)), the `<plaintext>` `media_type` hint, `<meta>` metadata (`original_timestamp`, `last_edit_timestamp_ms`, `poll_type`, `content_type`, `question_type`, `message_association_type`, `is_wamo_sub`, `admin_profile`), and the opaque `rcat` bytes. See [`NewsletterMessage`](/api/newsletter#newslettermessage) for the full field list.

<Note>
  `forwards_count`, `views_count`, and `responses_count` are `Option<u64>`. `None` means the server sent no counter, which is not the same as `Some(0)`. `views_count` and `responses_count` are typically only populated when the viewer's role in the channel entitles them to those figures.
</Note>

<Note>
  An edited message updates `timestamp` and carries `EditAttribute::AdminEdit` in `edit`; `last_edit_timestamp_ms` records the edit time in **milliseconds**, while every other timestamp on `NewsletterMessage` is in **seconds**. A revoked message carries `EditAttribute::AdminRevoke`, has an empty `<plaintext/>`, `message = None`, and no forward counter.
</Note>

### Pagination

Use the `server_id` from a previous response to paginate backwards:

```rust theme={null}
// Get messages before a specific server_id
let older = client.newsletter()
    .get_messages(&newsletter_jid, 20, Some(last_server_id))
    .await?;
```

See [Newsletter API reference](/api/newsletter#get_messages) for details.

## Live updates

Subscribe to real-time updates for a newsletter to receive changes to reaction counts, forward counts, and poll tallies:

```rust theme={null}
let duration = client.newsletter()
    .subscribe_live_updates(&newsletter_jid)
    .await?;

println!("Subscribed for {}s", duration);
```

The server sends `NewsletterLiveUpdate` events with the current counters of each changed message. Handle them in your event handler:

```rust theme={null}
use wacore::types::events::Event;

Event::NewsletterLiveUpdate(update) => {
    println!("Newsletter {} updated:", update.newsletter_jid);
    for msg in &update.messages {
        println!("  Message {}: {:?}", msg.server_id,
            msg.reactions.iter()
                .map(|r| format!("{} x{}", r.code, r.count))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        for vote in &msg.votes {
            println!("    poll option {}: {}", hex::encode(vote.option_hash), vote.count);
        }
        if let Some(forwards) = msg.forwards_count {
            println!("    forwards: {}", forwards);
        }
    }
}
```

Each update only includes messages whose counters changed. `votes` is empty for messages that aren't polls. Each tally is keyed by the same `option_hash` as the history tallies from `get_messages`. `forwards_count` is `None` when the server omits the counter. Live updates don't include `views_count` or `responses_count`.

<Note>
  The subscription duration (typically 300 seconds) is returned by the server. You need to re-subscribe periodically to continue receiving live updates.
</Note>

See [Events reference](/concepts/events#newsletterliveupdate) for the full event type.

## Error handling

Newsletter methods return `NewsletterError`. Match `NotFound` to detect a channel that doesn't exist:

```rust theme={null}
use whatsapp_rust::NewsletterError;

match client.newsletter().get_metadata(&jid).await {
    Ok(metadata) => println!("Found: {}", metadata.name),
    Err(NewsletterError::NotFound(jid)) => eprintln!("No channel at {}", jid),
    Err(NewsletterError::InvalidRequest(msg)) => eprintln!("Invalid request: {}", msg),
    Err(e) => eprintln!("Error: {}", e),
}
```

See [`NewsletterError`](/api/newsletter#error-handling) for all variants.

## Key differences from groups

| Feature | Newsletters | Groups |
| - | - | - |
| Encryption | Plaintext | Signal E2E |
| Messaging | One-way (admins only) | All members |
| JID server | `@newsletter` | `@g.us` |
| Reactions | Emoji counts (aggregated) | Per-message |
| API backend | MEX (GraphQL) | IQ stanzas |
